skill.name: controlnet-pose
skill.description: Routes pose-conditioned image and video requests through the RunComfy CLI. It helps choose Kling Motion Control, Wan Animate, or Z-Image ControlNet LoRA based on the reference media and desired output.
skill.summary: Generate pose-conditioned images and videos through RunComfy model routes.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are Markdown backticks, catalog URLs, or model-selection wording, not executable backtick syntax or reconnaissance. The meaningful residual risk is expected third-party processing of prompts and media URLs through RunComfy endpoints.

remediation.suggestion: Keep the explicit URL rule and add a consent reminder before submitting private media or non-public URLs to RunComfy.
Document how users can remove or rotate the RunComfy token, and prefer RUNCOMFY_TOKEN in ephemeral CI environments.
Keep tool permissions restricted to Bash(runcomfy *) and avoid adding npm, curl, or arbitrary shell commands to the skill.

content.value_statement: Pose and motion references are hard to route across video and image models. This skill selects RunComfy pose workflows and prepares CLI runs.
actual_capabilities: Routes video pose transfer to Kling Motion Control Pro or Standard.
Routes still-image pose conditioning to Z-Image Turbo ControlNet LoRA.
Explains Wan 2.2 Animate usage for stylized character animation.
Provides RunComfy CLI invocation patterns with structured inputs and output directories.
Points users to RunComfy ComfyUI workflows for multi-condition control stacks.
Lists exit codes and troubleshooting guidance for RunComfy CLI runs.
limitations: Requires RunComfy CLI installation and authentication before use.
Does not create OpenPose, DWPose, depth, or canny control images itself.
Sends prompts and media URLs to RunComfy model endpoints.
Multi-condition stacks require RunComfy ComfyUI workflows outside the CLI route.

use_cases.title: Transfer a Performance
use_cases.description: Map the motion from a reference video onto a target character image.

use_cases.title: Lock a Character Pose
use_cases.description: Create a still image that follows an OpenPose, DWPose, depth, or canny control image.

use_cases.title: Choose a Control Route
use_cases.description: Decide whether a request needs a CLI model endpoint or a RunComfy ComfyUI workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Pose-Locked Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this control image URL to create a character in the same pose. Choose the correct RunComfy image route.

prompt_templates.title: Transfer Motion to a Character
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this reference video and target character image to create a video with matching motion and blocking.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a pose reference and a desired output type. Recommend the best RunComfy route and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Condition Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a RunComfy workflow for pose plus depth control. Identify when the CLI route is insufficient.

output_examples.input: I have a dance reference video and a character portrait.
output_examples.output: Use Kling Motion Control Pro for final video transfer. Provide the reference video URL and character image URL.

output_examples.input: I need a still image that follows an OpenPose skeleton.
output_examples.output: Use Z-Image Turbo ControlNet LoRA. Provide the control image URL and a clear visual prompt.

output_examples.input: I want pose control plus depth and a reference image.
output_examples.output: Use a RunComfy ComfyUI workflow instead of the CLI model route because multiple conditions are required.

best_practices: Provide only media URLs that the user explicitly wants to send to RunComfy.
Use clean, single-subject reference media with stable framing and no scene cuts.
Use Standard for drafts and Pro for final Kling motion-control output.
anti_patterns: Uploading private media before confirming consent and intended third-party processing.
Using video motion-transfer models for still-image pose control requests.
Expecting the CLI route to build complex multi-condition ControlNet workflows.

faq.question: Does this skill run models locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses RunComfy cloud model endpoints through the RunComfy CLI.

faq.question: What tools does it need?
faq.answer: It needs the RunComfy CLI, an authenticated RunComfy account, and URLs for the required media inputs.

faq.question: Can it create OpenPose skeletons?
faq.answer: No. Create pose, depth, or canny control images separately, then provide their URLs.

faq.question: Which route fits video motion transfer?
faq.answer: Use Kling Motion Control Pro for final output, or Standard for cheaper draft iteration.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What privacy boundary should I know?
faq.answer: Prompts and media URLs are sent to RunComfy endpoints. Use only inputs approved for that service.
